summary: This PR swaps the template greeting for a Quiz screen: a scrolling list of 10 cards, each with a three-state checkbox, plus Android Studio project files. The UI builds fine. The main problem is that each answer is held only in temporary composable memory (`remember`), so answers are lost when the screen rotates or a card scrolls off and back.

accepted.title: Quiz answers are wiped when the user rotates the phone or scrolls
accepted.whatGoesWrong: A user ticks a few checkboxes, then rotates the device or switches to dark mode. Every checkbox goes back to the indeterminate state. On a small screen, scrolling a card out of view and back also resets it, because the lazy list throws away that item's remembered state when it leaves the screen.
accepted.whyItMatters: Users silently lose the answers they gave, which defeats the point of a quiz screen.
accepted.howToFix: Use `rememberSaveable` instead of `remember` for each item's state. A better option is to move the 10 answers into a list kept by the caller or a ViewModel, indexed by question, and pass each state and its change handler down to the cards.

accepted.title: Committed IDE settings point to a JDK that exists only on the author's machine
accepted.whatGoesWrong: `misc.xml` names a local JDK (`jbr-25`). `deploymentTargetSelector.xml` holds the author's own device picker. When another developer opens the project, the IDE may report a missing SDK, or the shared files may keep changing in diffs.
accepted.whyItMatters: These files cause noisy diffs and setup friction for other contributors, and they have nothing to do with the feature.
accepted.howToFix: Remove `.idea/misc.xml` and `.idea/deploymentTargetSelector.xml` from this PR and add them to `.gitignore`. Only commit IDE files the team actually means to share.
